notes.title: Monthly Update #29
notes.content:
Hey everyone, sorry for the lack of updates recently, haven't had anything too exciting to show off as I slowly tick away at the remainder of the game. We're going to be changing the cadence of these devlogs so we can put a bit more in them and increase our focus on building better things long term rather than crunching on little features to make for exciting changelogs each week.

For this months update, we have a new Environment System built into the game! Currently it stores a grid of information about the localised environment, such as temperature. If you place a fire, it can heat up the area around it and turn water into steam! This more energetic form of water can be used to push level elements around, and will eventually cool down and condense back into water.

You can see the environment grid by turning on Debug Mode, which will show hotter areas in red.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44311688/b0a8980db86b4e49bfad9c44da4fd31be5492307.png[/img]

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*]     New Flame level element
[*]     New Environment System
[*]         Water when heated up will turn into steam
[*]         This steam carries heat away from the source and will heat up the area it travels to, allowing for multi-stage steam boilers/condensers to be built
[*]         Once the steam has cooled down sufficiently (either through a water reservoir or by traveling through cooler air), it will condense back into water
[/list]

notes.content:
Hey all,

We've finally finished our new collision resolution system, that utilises hashmaps to improve collision performance by over 10x! Now we have extra headroom for more complex physical simulations, and can have considerably more particles in a given level.

A new fire/heat system is in progress to utilise the new system, keep an eye out in the future for that!

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*]     Reimplemented collision resolution to use a spatial hashmap, similar to food searching
[/list]

notes.title: Weekly Update #26
notes.content:
We forgot to post the last weeks update! We've been deep in the optimisation mines so that we can expand the number of entities in a level beyond 500 without slowing down, so that we can add some basic thermodynamics! The goal is to add fire particles that will add a heat value to a grid, which will diffuse and spread over time. This, in tandem with a new wood wall type, will allow for the propagation of fire, and the heating of water, which will add more interesting physics based level mechanics (like boiling water into steam to push something)!

Also, the tamagotchi mode is coming along too, as the FUNG is fed it becomes happier and slowly evolves into more calm behaviours, and a hungry FUNG becomes more ferocious. It'll stay persistent across sessions, unless you let it die and start again.

To keep y'all happy while I continue to improve performance, have a look at 4,000 water particles running somewhat more smoothly than before! (Note the spatial grid is now smaller, since hash lookups are cheap and circle-circle collisions are... less so) The maximum limit before these changes was only 400 water particles at a time

notes.title: Weekly Update #23
notes.content:
Hello once again, I hope you all had a great Christmas, surrounded by people that you love!

Next week, on Friday, we'll be releasing the first half of Chapter 2 (15 levels), instead of the planned whole chapter (20 levels). This is because we've decided to fill the chapter with more puzzles that we developed during playtests, and to further flesh out the story. The gap from this first half of the chapter to the second will not be anywhere near as long as the gap between chapter 1 and 2, since we already have all the design elements ready to go.

The upside to this, is you'll get 10 more puzzles, and they'll be considerably more difficult than everything faced so far. If you want to get to the bottom of the apparent self-immolation of the world, you'll need guts and brains.

notes.title: Weekly Update #21
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44311688/39808ba3bd88de250a5170a8e3e00edadc803acd.png[/img]

Not all things go to plan, especially in games development. Even with the blistering pace of work over the last 3 weeks, we're still a little behind on the release of the second chapter. On the upside, we've managed to eliminate all known bugs in the new mechanics, and catch quite a few unknown ones in the process! The bridge building tools have been playtested thoroughly, and have been reworked to be easier to understand and use. We have also been extensively playtesting the levels developed so far (about 19 levels), and tuning them so that they're difficult without being unfair.

We're sorry for the delay, but we're not going to release anything unfinished or untested, our respect for our audience extends to the quality of our gameplay, and we want you to feel that you're getting your time and money's worth. Not all is lost however, today's update is probably the last code change required for Chapter 2!

Our plan was to take a 2 week break after the 22nd to recharge over the Christmas break. Instead, we're going to finish this off over those 2 weeks and release Chapter 2: COLLAPSE on the 5th of January, and then we'll take a break! Don't feel too bad for me though, I honestly love the process of making games, it's been a fantastic year of triumphs in both Drift King and FUNG. Also we don't have any employees yet, so I'm only burning my own time off, I wouldn't dare force crunch upon anyone else.

notes.title: Weekly Update #18
notes.content:
Drift on, drift 'til you drop, be the envy of Glandeen the Drift Pig himself.

Introducing the most sophisticated drift racing AI ever developed, coming straight to you in Alpha v0.8! This one has been in the works for quite a while now, and finally it has paid off. This drift model uses no neural nets, prerecorded inputs, or any other trickery - to bring you an unparalleled single player racing experience! It has been designed using a simple state machine and just a smidge of calculus.

Since this isn't directly related to FUNG, I'll leave the meat of this out, but if you're interested in reading more, check out the Drift King devlog: https://mellowarpeggiation.itch.io/drift-king/devlog/640000/weekly-update-18-the-machine-revolution-begins


Happy drifting!

- George

notes.title: Weekly Update #8

[h3]BOOM[/h3]
That's the sound of your last tower succumbing to the FUNG. Your final defense against the onslaught of green, laid to waste. In your final moments, you think to yourself...

[i]Damn... that was pretty fun actually, not gonna lie[/i]

You are the latest victim in the NEW TOWER DEFENSE GAMEMODE available now!

This week, we added a new gamemode to FUNG - Tower Defense - which generates random levels for you to survive many waves against the FUNG in. Currently, it's in a very early stage of implementation, but since it's already quite fun, we decided to release it for you all now! It ain't called Early Access for nothing!

Introducing, the FUNG Demo! Including the first half of Chapter One - DESCENT, to give you a good feel for what to expect from the full game. The demo is available for free on Steam and itch.io from today!

In other news, we've added a bunch of new story telling elements to the level editor, including subscenes (useful for making interactable computer terminals), and character portraits. No longer will you be spoken to only through a radio, you'll be accompanied throughout Chapter Two - COLLAPSE by the tough and resourceful Red!
[img]https://i.ibb.co/ngkkm5M/Screenshot-2023-08-24-155729.png[/img]

Alongside the new story telling elements, we've also added another physics object, based on the bridge building parts, the water wheel! It's still being worked on so don't be alarmed if it's a little janky.
[img]https://i.ibb.co/qmr7Mcn/water-wheel.png[/img]

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*] Added Subscenes, can be triggered from Points of Interest (PoIs)
[*] Added text input configuration for Points of Interest, can set a password to trigger a subscene to open
[*] Rearranged bridge tools in the level editor to save space, now a single tool builds all parts
[*] Note that the tools are still split for players, keeping it simple and easy to use
[*] Added Computer UI Elements
[*] Currently, only the computer Bootscreen is available
[*] Added Water Wheels, useful for moving water around
[*] Added link to the Discord from the main menu
[*] Added character portraits, create your portraits as a 640x360 .png, and add them to your level intro dialogue
[*] These are saved per chapter, so you only need to add your images once to use them anywhere within the chapter
[*] Fix character portraits not being rendered at the same pixel scale as the game (even less mixels!)
[/list]

notes.title: Weekly Update #4 - Let Me Level With You
notes.content:
Hi how are ya? This week has been a focus on end user experience (and fixing a lot of bugs!) for both FUNG and Drift King. Yes, I said in the last update that we wouldn't touch Drift King for a while but we ended up working on it in our spare time, and fortunately y'all get to enjoy the fruits of our labour (that, and there were some game breaking bugs that I didn't want to leave in the public build!)

For FUNG, we've implemented a new level style selector, so you can spruce up your levels without having to import a custom FG/BG from an image editor. In terms of new content, the focus has been on creating the levels for Chapter Two - COLLAPSE, but I can give you a sneak peek of one of the levels - WITNESS - as shown in the attached screenshot. So far, concepts for about 8 levels have been sketched out, out of the planned 30 for the chapter.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/X4t07Zd/Screenshot-2023-08-15-154836.png[/img]

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*] Added new visual styles for levels
[*] 	Tiedye - the default style from the initial Steam launch
[*] 	Classic - the style from the LOVE JAM 2023 entry
[*] 	Eighties - A more aesthetic style
[*] 	Descent - A style that more closely mimics the style of Chapter One
[*] Reworked levels D-8 and D-18 to use the new autogenerated visual styles
[*] Reworked the custom chapter LOVE JAM 2023 to use the new Classic style
[*] Prevent bridge parts being created within walls, preventing players breaking levels by effectively creating their own anchor points
[*] Explosions now destroy bridge parts
[/list]

And that's all for this week. Have fun!

- George

notes.title: Weekly Update #3 - Maybe The Real Treasure Was The Bridges We Burned On The Way
notes.content:
[img]https://i.ibb.co/ZxH00dz/fung-bridge.png[/img]

Hey ho, hey ho, delivering the weekly update we go! FUNG is getting all the focus once again so we can hit our target of finishing the game in about 4 months. To that end we have added some more level mechanics and tools that will be present in Chapter Two - COLLAPSE
If you haven't yet figured out the theme of the next chapter from the title (and the stream of updates in our Discord), COLLAPSE is about physics puzzles and bridge building. So, starting off strong we have added a softbody simulation and four new tools:
[list]
[*] Bridges
[*] Walls
[*] Girders
[*] Ropes
[/list]

These tools should provide a wide array of potential puzzles alongside all the other level elements already present. If you can't wait for the chapter release in about 2 months time, don't worry, we've already got a very short taste tester level pack for you!
Those that have the game on Steam will be able to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3018263041]download the taster level pack from the Steam Workshop[/url] immediately! Itch.io users will find the level pack attached to this post and [url=https://discord.gg/GM5tPjqTsE]in the Discord[/url]!

If you're looking for updates on Drift King, this will be the last one you'll see for a little while yet, make sure to [url=https://mellowarpeggiation.itch.io/]follow us on itch.io[/url] for any future updates. Drift King is our favourite project and it's going to take a lot of strength to keep it on the backburner, so who knows, it might get a sneaky update or two in between work on FUNG.

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*] Added rigid softbody Walls and Bridges
[*] Added fully rigid Girders
[*] Added flexible Ropes
[*] Bridge parts have a strain limit, if too much tension is applied they'll snap
[*] Remove "mixels", hoses now render at the same pixel scale as the level
[*] Added shadows to some level elements to improve visibility
[/list]

We'd love to see your creations with these new tools, so submit them to the Workshop and the Discord, we'll feature all the ones that we enjoy.

- George

notes.title: Weekly Update #2 - Contractual Observations
notes.content:
Greetings, once again, to the WARDENS and the Drift Elite, and welcome to the second weekly update!
This week has had a different flow than most, considering that our lead (and only) developer has been busy working on contract for a previous employer for most of the week. But we gave him extra carrots in exchange for using some of his spare time to get you some quality of life updates, bug fixes, and new functionality!
We've also started on the visual design of the second chapter of FUNG: COLLAPSE, as shown in the screenshot below.

FUNG - Changelog:

[*] Light shadows now update in real-time as you dig, making it much easier to tell when a light is properly blocked/unblocked
[*] Lights now have a subtle halo showing at what distance their influence no longer applies

notes.title: Weekly Update #1 - Sudden Weeklies!
notes.content:
​Greetings WARDENS and the Drift Monarchy, today marks the first week of weekly updates! Each Friday we will be updating you all on progress on our various games, make sure to follow us or join our [url=https://discord.gg/KXfe8TQugK]community Discord[/url]​ to not miss out on any cool new features!

This week has had a short shift in focus to make some progress on Drift King, slowly inching forwards towards true multiplayer, fleshing out the final feature set of the game, and building the huge open world of Drift City. You may not be able to race each other just yet, but at least you can now communicate with each other!

Not all has been Drift King however, a bugfix release for FUNG has been completed, fixing all the issues brought to our attention during the first week of play. Some improvements to the FUNG GoL rendering have also been made, which should be very noticeable on the title screen!

FUNG - Changelog:
[list]
[*] Improved FUNG GoL rendering - should appear less blocky in the center
[*] Fixed crash when resetting a level that has had a secret added
[*] Fixed crash when physics enabled objects went through terrain and offscreen in a single frame
[/list]

This concludes our first weekly update, feedback is - as ever - much appreciated! Go ahead and grab the latest versions and get playing!

- George
